title: NORM.S.INV uses AS241 tails (p < 0.075 and p > 15/16) and three x87-stored rational/Padé pieces for sqrt(2)*erfinv(2p-1) in between
statement: Excel's standard normal inverse (NORM.S.INV and NORMSINV) partitions (0, 1) asymmetrically: Wichura's AS241 formula runs for p < 0.075 and p > 15/16 using x87 FYL2X + FSQRT stored sqrt(-ln v), while the middle computes sqrt(2) * erfinv(t) with t = 2*(p - 0.5) across three pieces: for s = RN(t*t) <= 0.5, a degree-7/7 rational interpolant at the 15 zeros of T15 on [0, 0.73] solved near 100-bit precision; for sqrt(0.5) < |t| <= 0.85, a degree-7/5 rational interpolant times sqrt(-ln(1 - |t|)); and for 0.85 < t <= 0.875 (p in (0.925, 15/16]), a degree-9/9 Padé approximant centred at 225/256 solved at 96-bit precision times sqrt(-ln(1 - t)), storing every Horner product and sum from x87 64-bit precision to binary64. NORM.INV/NORMINV return mu + sigma*z, LOGNORM.INV/LOGINV return EXP(mu + sigma*z), and CONFIDENCE/CONFIDENCE.NORM return NORM.S.INV(1 - alpha/2)*sigma/SQRT(size) with stored steps. See https://github.com/DnaCalc/DnaCalc/blob/4fb9b728df8a96546ae685589b47e057b7e26771/docs/articles/last-bit-normsinv.md.
basis: Matched across 21,898 of 21,898 full-bank witness rows across all eight functions in Excel 16.0.20527 (NORMSINV 2,210/2,210, NORM.S.INV 2,206/2,206, NORM.INV 2,915/2,915, NORMINV 2,914/2,914, LOGNORM.INV 2,911/2,911, LOGINV 2,916/2,916, CONFIDENCE 2,910/2,910, CONFIDENCE.NORM 2,916/2,916), plus 32,452 of 32,452 frozen piece-C inputs and 1,230,456 distinct sweep inputs (docs/articles/last-bit-normsinv.md).
inferred: The exact polynomial solve precisions (~100 bits for piece A and 96 bits for piece C) and compiled code structure are inferred from output-bit discriminators (such as p = 0x3fed999bc5f0efd8) and frozen holdout runs rather than source inspection.
